chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washsha, who said: 'I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying:'

'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said to the disciples: 'O Children of Israel! Do not despair over what has passed from you of the world, just as the people of the world do not despair over what has passed from them of their religion, as long as they attain their world.'
ai.seo_question: What is the comparison made between losing the world and losing religion?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrates that Prophet 'Isa (Jesus) (peace be upon him) advised the Children of Israel not to grieve over worldly losses, drawing a parallel to how worldly people remain unconcerned about losing their religion as long as they secure their material wealth. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the Shia concept of *ghurur* (deception) of the world, illustrating that the attachment to dunya often blinds believers to the loss of their deen, a theme central to the chapter on condemning the world.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha who said, 
‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘Isa<sup>as</sup> Bin Maryam<sup>as</sup> said to the disciples: ‘O Children of Israel! Do not despair upon what is lost by you from the world, just as the people of the world do not despair upon what is lost by them from their Religion as long as they secure their world’.
en.sarwar: 25. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ who has said the following: “I heard al-Rida (a.s.) say,

‘Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) said to his disciples, “O Israelites, do not regret for what you may miss of the world, just as the people of the world (who have no religion) do not regret for what they miss of religion when they find their worldly materials.’”
